subject: english
title: Nine Gold Medals
author: David Roth
instructions: Literature practice for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Identify the following sentences as True or False.

questions.q: The athletes came from all over the country.
When the smallest athlete fell, none of the others even looked at him.
The hundred-yard race had eight winners.
The eight other runners turned around and went back to help the fallen boy.
The runners finished the race holding hands.
The spectators were silent at the end of the race.

sections.title: Match the character (or speaker) with the description.

questions.right: cried out in frustration and anguish when his dreams were 'dashed in the dirt'
questions.answer: The smallest runner — cried out in frustration and anguish when his dreams were 'dashed in the dirt'

questions.right: turned back to help the fallen boy
questions.answer: The eight other runners — turned back to help the fallen boy

questions.right: gathered around the old field to cheer the young athletes
questions.answer: The spectators — gathered around the old field to cheer the young athletes

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The race began when the ________ exploded.
The smallest runner stumbled and ________.
He fell to the ________.

sections.passage:
The signal was given, the pistol exploded
And so did the runners all charging ahead
But the smallest among them, he stumbled and staggered
And fell to the asphalt instead.

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The race ended with nine ________ medals.
They came to the finish line holding ________.
The audience gave them a standing ________.

sections.passage:
That's how the race ended, with nine gold medals
They came to the finish line holding hands still
And a standing ovation and nine beaming faces
Said more than these words ever will.

questions.q: The final event of the day was the ________ dash.
There were ________ resolved athletes behind the starting line.
The banner above said ________.
The poem 'Nine Gold Medals' was written by ________.

sections.title: Answer in one or two sentences (about 30 words).

questions.q: How did the race in the poem 'Nine Gold Medals' end?
questions.answer: All nine runners joined hands and walked to the finish line together. They all got gold medals and received a standing ovation.

questions.q: The nine athletes were lined up to run which race?
questions.answer: They were lined up for the hundred-yard dash, the final event of the day.

questions.q: What made the eight runners suddenly stop?
questions.answer: The smallest runner stumbled and fell to the asphalt. Seeing him cry out in frustration, the eight others stopped, turned back and helped him up.

questions.q: Why did the authorities award gold medals to all nine athletes?
questions.answer: All nine crossed the finish line together, holding hands, after the eight had helped the fallen runner; their kindness made them all winners.

questions.q: How did the spectators react when all nine reached the finishing line?
questions.answer: They gave the runners a standing ovation, and the nine faces were beaming with joy.

questions.q: What message do we get from the poem 'Nine Gold Medals'?
questions.answer: Human values such as empathy, cooperation and helping others are more important than winning; when we help each other, everyone wins.

questions.q: Explain the significance of the title 'Nine Gold Medals'.
questions.answer: Only one runner normally wins gold in a race, but here all nine finished together after the eight turned back to help the fallen boy. Each deserved gold for kindness and sportsmanship, so the title shows that compassion made all of them winners.

or.q: How did the hundred-yard race end with nine gold medals?
or.answer: The smallest runner fell; the other eight stopped, went back and helped him to his feet. Then all nine joined hands and walked to the finish line together, so all of them were given gold medals amid a standing ovation.
